current.text: Charlotte acquired him in the LaMelo Ball trade.
He is set to start at power forward and takes the spot of Miles Bridges, who was traded. Moussa Diabate is the projected starting center.
Charlotte has several centers (Diabate, Kalkbrenner, Kai Jones, a first-round rookie), so he may play more power forward than center.
He should play the most minutes of his career, about 31 to 33 per game.
With Ball and Bridges gone, Charlotte has a lot of open usage, and his shots should go up.
Experts put him in the mid rounds, at about rank 55 to 75. The newest note says he has been underwhelming but is being drafted in the right spot. One expert says he goes earlier in category leagues.
Experts disagree on his upside. One sees a better chance of a top 50 finish than of falling outside the top 100. Others see no upside above his mid-round tier and say he is not as good as the hype.
In an auction mock draft he went for 14 USD. The drafter had hoped to get him for about 10 USD.
Charlotte plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes, and its playmaking will be spread across several players.

durable.text: He is a very good floor spacer for a big and can play the four or the five.
Threes and blocks are his best categories. He makes far more threes than most forwards and centers. His FG% is below average for his position.
He is a bad defender. His shooting is up and down, and his scoring can be inefficient.
He is not a strong fantasy center. He does not boost FG% and does not give big rebound numbers.
He has not yet shown that he can handle a big usage load.
He has missed very few games in each of the last three seasons.

note: Reid went for 2 USD in our league last season. This year the markets split: the Yahoo average cost is 4 USD and the ESPN average cost is 13 USD, and in a mock auction he went for 14 USD. The expert consensus is a mid-round player (rank about 55 to 75), so a price of about 10 to 14 USD is fair, and he is a good fit for builds that want threes and blocks from a F/C without needing a FG% boost. Early in the season, check that he really plays 31 or more minutes at power forward and that his shot volume rises above the 11.3 attempts he took last season.
